newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends at 14-month high vs dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends at 14-month high vs dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended up at a 14-month high close of 8.3003 on Tuesday from Monday's 8.3007 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market due to strong pro-yuan sentiment, traders said.
The previous high was 8.3001 on August 7, 1995.
The yuan opened higher at 8.3003 and fluctuated widely for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.3000 in early trading and a low of 8.3023 late in the session.
Trading was much more active than on Monday with most done at 8.3005, traders said.
Traders said there was a fierce battle between yuan buyers and sellers just below the key 8.3000 resistance level.

"Sellers wanted to push the yuan below the 8.3010 level to prevent it breaking through the key resistance," a trader said. "They failed due to strong pro-yuan sentiment but succeeded in making the yuan close below the resistance level."

Most traders agree that the yuan is likely to break through the key resistance shortly due to strong pro-yuan sentiment supported by China's continued rising foreign exchange reserves and an expected large surplus in foreign trade this year.
"The yuan hit an intra-day high of 8.3000 today, indicating the breakthrough is not far away," said a second trader.
Traders expect the yuan to move around 8.3000 on Wednesday.
The yuan closed down at 7.4500 from 7.4180 against 100 Japanese yen on Tuesday and up at 1.0736 from 1.0741 against the Hong Kong dollar.
